keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Xiaoheyan row. The page gives no area. Its infobox is 'c. 3000-2500BC' (range 'Aohan Banner, Inner Mongolia'), its lead and body 'approximately 3500-2000 BC'; the Hongshan and Lower Xiajiadian infoboxes give 'Xiaoheyan (3000-2000 BCE)', so 3000 to 2000 is used. The early extent ('throughout the northern and southern regions of Yanshan Mountain', 'Zhangjiakou and Datong in the west, and Shijiazhuang in the south') has no year on the page; it is drawn from the start (confidence 1) because the page ties it to the culture's early stage (the fourth stage of Banpo to the second stage of Miaodigou). The shape is the Chifeng 100 km core disc plus the early extent minus the Hongshan land, 1,092 cells, about 276,000 km2 by the gazetteer.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'in the later Longshan period' the Xiaoheyan 'at the southern foot of Yanshan was replaced by the Hougang second stage culture' while 'the area north of Yanshan remains the Xiaoheyan culture'. The year is bridged (confidence 1): the Longshan page dates 'The late period (2600 to 2000 BC) of the Longshan culture' and Miaodigou II to '3000 to 2600 BC', and the Xiaoheyan page's early stage ends with Miaodigou II. 'North of Yanshan' is read as the West Liao basin and Chengde: 720 cells, about 182,000 km2. Zhangjiakou and Datong are dropped with the south; the page does not say whether the west also fell.

notes:
Xiaoheyan culture (3000-2000 BCE, West Liao basin and Yanshan), typed culture like its predecessor hongshan-culture; Cliopatria has no row. Four pages opened.

To settle: (1) Dates disagree on the Xiaoheyan page itself (infobox c. 3000-2500 BC; lead and body about 3500-2000 BC); 3000 to 2000 is taken from the Hongshan and Lower Xiajiadian infoboxes and matches the infobox start and the lead end. (2) The page's geography (Yanshan north and south, to Zhangjiakou, Datong and Shijiazhuang in an undated 'early stage') is much larger than the Hongshan-based area the request expected; the Chifeng-Chaoyang shape is added at -2900 from the Hongshan, and the wide early extent is drawn from -3000 at confidence 1. It overlaps the longshan-culture dossier (Shanxi, southern Hebei) and the Hongshan 3000-2900; the size rule or a ruling is needed. (3) The 2600 contraction to north of Yanshan is bridged from the Longshan page's 2600 to 2000 late period (confidence 1); the longshan-culture dossier holds only Handan in Hebei, so the Xiaoheyan's loss at -2600 has no matching gain and the lost land (northern Hebei) is Longshan only per the Xiaoheyan page. (4) The Lower Xiajiadian culture (2200-1600 BC; southeastern Inner Mongolia, northern Hebei, western Liaoning) has no dossier and starts 200 years before the Xiaoheyan ends: gap-filler needed (suggested slug lower-xiajiadian-culture). (5) The Lower Xiajiadian page lists the Xiaoheyan as 'transitional' and the page gives no hand-over event. (6) Native name 小河沿文化 is the standard Chinese name, not read from the page text returned. (7) No gazetteer names are needed (Chifeng, Chaoyang, Chengde, Zhangjiakou, Datong, Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei all resolve); Aohan and Xinhui are absent from the gazetteer and the Chifeng 100 km disc stands for Aohan Banner.
